idea_name: Rolling past-vs-future mean-move Pearson mean-reversion map
mechanism: From EURUSD H1 closes form bar diffs; compute last rolling means over windows 2–23 and next rolling means over horizons 2–9 (future means shifted to avoid leakage); Pearson corr heatmap of past means vs future means. Peak negative corr ≈−0.02…−0.03 in mid windows (≈8–14 past × 5–8 future) → weak structured mean reversion; short/long windows drown or blur.
data_needed: OHLCV via mt5.copy_rates_range; close series; UTC-aligned datetime.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 from 2020-01-01 to present (article run)
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a concrete multi-horizon inertia/mean-reversion regime map (not single lag-1 corr) with explicit mid-range sweet spot and leakage-safe future windows.
quote: In the central region of the matrix (windows of 8–14 bars in history and 5–8 bars in the horizon), the effect intensifies and reaches the values of −0.02…−0.03. This is a weak but consistent mean reversion signal.

mechanism: Build feature matrix from last/next diffs, last_mean_11 and gaps, plus SMA/RSI/MACD over periods {4,8,12,24,36,48} and their first and second diffs (D*, DD*); also MACD signal/main gaps and diffs. Keep only features whose max |Pearson| vs next_* targets ≥0.02.
data_needed: Close series; ta SMA/RSI/MACD families; rolling/diff transforms; dropna.
why_new_for_mis: Treats second-order (acceleration) transforms of classic indicators as first-class predictive features with an explicit correlation floor—feature-space sensing recipe for MIS, not just raw RSI/MACD levels.
quote: The addition of second-order derivatives is especially indicative (diff and diff from diff). This is already an attempt to capture the change in the signal itself - a transition to the analysis of the acceleration and deceleration of market movement.

idea_name: RF next_9 move with train-percentile |pred| confidence filter
mechanism: RandomForestRegressor on selected features (last, last_11, last_last_11, SMA_12, multi-MACD set) predicts sum of next 9 bar moves; chronological 90/10 split; tune n_estimators/max_depth(/max_leaf_nodes) by test pred–target corr. Then thresholds = percentiles of |pred_train|; on test, trade only if |pred|≥threshold, position=sign(pred)*sign(corr), subtract fixed cost 0.00021; pick threshold by equity/win_rate. Export to ONNX and mirror features in MQL5 OnTick/IsNewBar.
data_needed: EURUSD H1 closes; feature vector matching training order; ONNX model; threshold from train percentiles.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; Strategy Tester Q1 2026 on EURUSD_i
why_new_for_mis: MIS can use absolute model confidence (train |pred| percentile) as a live gate on a weak-edge sequence/regression sensor—noise abstain rather than always-on direction.
quote: ignore weak signals and work only where the model demonstrates sufficient confidence or the expected movement covers the costs. This is already a transition from the function model to the trading filter model.

idea_name: GPU candlestick shape-similarity outcome sensor (TP×SL grid)
mechanism: Encode each bar as float4 OHLC; reference = last PATTERN_SIZE candles; scan history comparing body, upper shadow, lower shadow within tolerance; on match simulate buy/sell from next open over horizon bars with worst-case SL-first, time-forced exit; aggregate match count and TP/SL hit rates for every (tp,sl) on a 3D OpenCL grid; EA opens only if sample size adequate and buy vs sell probabilities favor a side.
data_needed: OHLC history arrays; PATTERN_SIZE; tolerance; horizon; tp[]/sl[] grids; OpenCL PatternStats3D kernel.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: generic MT5 symbol/TF in PatternStats.mq5 test EA (article charts)
why_new_for_mis: Similarity-based path sensor: current candle geometry → empirical conditional hit probabilities across a TP/SL lattice, without named textbook patterns—statistical lookalike regime for MIS.
quote: Instead of looking up familiar figures from textbooks in advance, you can approach the problem differently. Do not force ready-made templates on the market, but look at how it has behaved in similar situations before.

mechanism: OO CONNXPredictor binds shapes, min-max normalizes live features with training scaler bounds, OnnxRun once per new bar. Article stresses markets shift between low-vol mean-reversion and high-vol momentum, causing out-of-sample decay; operators must monitor predictive accuracy and retrain/replace ONNX when drift appears.
data_needed: ONNX file; fixed-size feature vector; training min/max; rolling prediction vs realized outcomes for drift checks.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: generic chart symbol PERIOD_CURRENT (EA example uses iClose features)
why_new_for_mis: Frames neural-sensor lifecycle as an explicit regime-change problem: accuracy decay under vol/mean-reversion↔momentum shifts is the sensing/ops signal, not only the raw OnnxRun score.
quote: Financial markets undergo continuous regime changes, shifting aggressively between low-volatility mean reversion phases and high-volatility momentum phases. A neural network trained on a specific historical dataset will inevitably suffer from out-of-sample decay

idea_name: SLSQP-fitted GARCH-family conditional volatility parity with Python ARCH
mechanism: Port Dieter Kraft SLSQP (CSlsqp + CFunctor/CConstraints, analytic or FD gradients, box+inequality constraints, KKT active-set) into HARX/ARCH fit under __SLSQP__; maximize log-likelihood for MEAN_CONSTANT + VOL_{GARCH,GJR_GARCH,TARCH,AVGARCH,ARCH,...} with stationarity/non-negativity constraints. Yields parameters and LL matching Python arch within numerical tolerance (vs divergent ALGLIB minNLC fits).
data_needed: return/price series from MT5; model spec P/O/Q/Power; starting values/backcast; constraint matrices.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: MT5 sample pulls compared to Python ARCH (VolatilityModelParameterComparison); symbol/TF user-configurable in scripts
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a native, Python-parity conditional-vol sensor stack (GARCH family) with trustworthy MLE—usable as live σ̂_t / residual / LL features rather than mismatched ALGLIB estimates.
quote: By porting SLSQP to MQL5 and wiring it into the HARX fitting pipeline ... the MQL5 volatility library now reproduces Python ARCH results reproducibly: parameter estimates and log‑likelihoods match the Python reference within practical numerical tolerances
